assumptions: Probe starts are spaced 1/rate apart across the whole run (the rate limiter), so the minimum is (probes - 1) / rate. It assumes every probe answers instantly.
Probes that get no answer hold a concurrency slot until the timeout. The 'all time out' figure assumes every probe does, so the slower of the rate limit and the concurrency limit decides the time.
Real runs fall between the two. Event-loop scheduling, DNS, and timer granularity (about 15.6 ms ticks on Windows with Python 3.11/3.12) add small deviations.
Raising concurrency does not speed up a run whose pace is set by the rate limit.
